abstract: The replication initiation proteins (Reps) encoded by Staphylococcus aureus pathogenicity islands (SaPIs) are helicases that recognize their own origins of replication (oris). Despite their ability to melt the cognate ori without accessory proteins, the nature of the transition from origin-loaded to actively unwinding states remains poorly understood. Here, we report crystal and cryo-EM structures of the SaPIbov1 Rep, a homohexameric superfamily 6 (SF6) helicase, in apo and nucleotide plus duplex DNA-bound states. Comparison to superfamily 3 (SF3) SaPI Reps and archaeal/eukaryotic MCMs reveals differing structural adaptations for DNA engagement. Notably, SaPIbov1 Rep retains pore-loop 1 (PL1) and the pre-sensor 1 {beta}-hairpin (PS1) for DNA-binding, but lacks the Helix-2 insertion (H2i) conserved in MCM helicases and instead possesses an elongated PS1 providing extended DNA contact. 3D variability analysis (3DVA) resolved multiple ring-open conformational intermediate states, with ring asymmetry correlating to DNA binding. The duplex-bound single hexamer captured here likely represents a pre-replicative intermediate preceding double hexamer assembly. We also show that the disordered N-terminus of SaPIbov1 Rep binds its cognate primase and predict that the primase recruits the host DNA polymerase III.
